Certificate: equal verified isometry signatures; the unverified signature is computed first for every candidate of a cluster (hashes in data/filling_usig.jsonl) and the verified one only where unverified signatures agree or are missing (budget choice). State 2026-11-13 07:00: the search on this slope set is complete: every candidate filling has an unverified signature (295,871 hashes, no failure). 138,378 of the clusters consist of knots of one mutation class (classes of the mu pass; mutants have fillings of equal volume at corresponding slopes): no two signatures agree in any of them. The other 374 clusters give 286 hyperbolic coincidences (84 at the same slope, 47 at slopes p/q and -p/q, 155 at different slopes; 253 closed manifolds, 223 knots); with the 42 by name the file has 328 records. History: up to the stage 6a checkpoint the exports had 68 hyperbolic coincidences, found under a time budget on a smaller slope set; the check-in of 2026-11-12 22:12 had 142 (full slope set); 134 more involve fillings whose filled triangulation has no positively oriented solution (see geometric solutions) and 10 more came from the hard retry of failed signatures; the stage 6c checkpoint has all 286. Audit (scripts/audit_coincidences.py, data/coincidence_audit.json): for the 35 prime knots with at most 8 crossings the verified signature of every filling of the slope set was computed with no filter (60 randomisations, Regina with 60 s on the rest); the classes of equal signature are the 25 classes the pipeline has on these knots, no class is split by the volume or the unverified-signature filter, and SnapPy's isometry checker finds no isometric pair among fillings with equal |p|, close volume and different signatures (there is no such pair); 11 fillings stay without geometric solution and without lens or Seifert name (degenerate solutions; Regina names 10 of them as graph manifolds). Lens-space pairs are not written as S1 records: F10 gives both equations on each filling. Further checks (2026-11-12): for 200 random candidates the filling -p/q of the mirror, built from a re-drawn mirror diagram, has the same unverified signature in all 200 cases; for 150 random fillings the volume from such a second triangulation differs by at most 5e-10. Orientation: a coincidence is a homeomorphism of fillings that may reverse orientation (isometry signatures with ignore_orientation, lens and Seifert names normalised up to orientation); candidates are matched on |p|. The mirror identities S_{-p/q}(K*) = -S_{p/q}(K) are not coincidences: fillings exist for one chirality of each knot with slopes of both signs, and mirror nodes are reached through F3/C3. Counting: the 1,059 records written up to the stage 4+5 checkpoint include 922 that name the same torus knot twice at the same slope (T(p,q) and its table name; the solver drops them) and 2 that compare p/q with -p/q on the amphichiral knot 4_1; they form 98 classes of fillings, i.e. 110 independent equations (68 hyperbolic, 42 by name). From 2026-11-12 scripts/find_coincidences.py writes only those. Search-key changes of 2026-11-13 (three engineering agents studied the step; their scripts and tables are in /home/user/mrcalc_scratch/agents): (1) the unverified signature is computed by mrcalc/fastsig.py, the same algorithm and the same string as SnapPy's isometry_signature(verified=False) with a scalar inner loop (0.15 instead of about 0.6 CPU-s per filling; identical strings on 568 fillings, the 25 audit classes and 40 mirror pairs; tests/test_fastsig.py compares it with SnapPy on every test run and must pass after any SnapPy upgrade); (2) the volume tolerance of the candidate clusters is 1e-8 instead of 2e-7 (volumes of two descriptions of one filling agreed to 1e-13 in 340 checked pairs and are recorded to 1e-9): 295,319 candidate fillings in 138,752 clusters, 374 of them outside a single mutation class, the same 328 coincidence records; (3) a failed signature is retried with 40 randomisations and higher precision, and a filling that still has none is compared with its cluster by SnapPy's isometry checker (none left); (4) considered and not used: homology of the covers of degree at most 5 as a further key (removes about a third of the mutation-class fillings at 0.04-0.06 CPU-s each, which no longer pays at 0.15 CPU-s per signature), Chern-Simons (splits no mutation-class cluster and, taken modulo 1/2, separated two certified coincidences), high-precision volume, length spectrum, Turaev-Viro (split nothing or cost as much as the signature). Wider slope set (2026-11-13, |p| <= 60, q <= 8 on the table knots): 1,143,597 candidate fillings in 537,301 clusters; the 1,140 clusters outside a mutation class were tested (1,632 unverified and 115 verified signatures): 345 hyperbolic coincidences, i.e. 59 more, on 35 knots with 4 to 13 crossings (new ones at q = 5, 6 and at |p| between 30 and 50; none at q = 7, 8), all 328 earlier records kept. Export layout and memory (2026-11-11): The export is packed: JSONL files are gzip parts of at most 40 MiB, chain files are members of chains/chains-NNN.tar.xz, knots.csv is continued in knots.N.csv, peripheral nodes are in knots_peripheral[.k].xlsx (FORMAT.md, "Parts and packing"). scripts/export_pack.py unpack restores the literal section-9 file names; the checker and route.py read both layouts.

incidents.what: convention run of the stage 6c checkpoint reported a failure that was not acted on
incidents.detail: The convention run at 00:50 UTC listed "cable surgery identity (sanity)" as failed: 8 homology agreements, 0 signature agreements. The test compared the signature of a cable filling with that of the companion filling whenever one random closed triangulation of the cable filling was positively oriented, and asked for at least 1 of 8; usually 1 or 2 were, in that run none (no two signatures disagreed). The orchestrator did not stop: its check searched the log for a word that a Python traceback of the command also contains. Both are corrected (the test retriangulates and uses the drilled redescription, 5 to 7 signatures of 8 in four runs, all equal; the check uses the exit status, from the first check-in after the stage 6c checkpoint). The test was re-run before the checkpoint results were used: it passes. All other convention tests passed in the 00:50 run. Earlier convention runs by the orchestrator could have missed a failure in the same way; the convention tests are also part of the test suite run at every full checkpoint, which passed each time.

All running jobs were lost: three shards of the k = 6 pass on 10 crossings after about 9 hours of work each (restarted from zero), the low-priority signature run (resumed from its cache) and a solve. Move passes now keep per-diagram progress of unfinished shards (mrcalc/passes.py, progress files outside the pass directory).
